explanation: A rectangle of width a and height (b + c) has area a(b + c). Split the height into a b-piece and a c-piece and you get two smaller rectangles of area a*b and a*c that together fill the SAME rectangle — that is why a(b + c) = ab + ac. Slide a to scale the width and slide b and c to set how the height splits; the sweeping highlight steps between the two pieces so you see each product the distribution creates.
bullets: a(b + c) means a copies of the whole sum b + c.
Distributing multiplies a by EACH term: a*b and a*c, then add.
The area model shows the two products tile the same rectangle as the whole.
